purpose: Design and verify distributed software behavior across nodes under delay, concurrency, partial failure, replication, retry, and partition while preserving network, product, infrastructure, and SRE ownership boundaries.

owns: Distributed-state protocols, consistency/availability tradeoffs, replication, coordination, idempotency, retry and partial-failure behavior.
Fault models, protocol invariants, trace reasoning, simulation/fault-injection evidence and distributed recovery contracts.
does_not_own: Physical/network infrastructure design, product consistency policy, infrastructure capacity authority, or SRE risk acceptance by default.
Claiming fault tolerance beyond the exact fault model and environments actually exercised.
escalates_when: A consistency or availability choice changes user/product semantics.
A protocol guarantee depends on network/infrastructure behavior or operational risk not directly evidenced by this package.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Preserve exact candidate/environment identity across work.
Stop or hand off when the decision exceeds professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute the same body using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute mechanical steps but must stop at unresolved judgment or observation boundaries.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence, authority, or tested scope.

reads: Accepted project/system state relevant to the profession.
Exact candidate, interfaces, dependencies and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded implementation/design/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs when another profession owns a decision.
coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; convenience does not transfer authority.
A technically successful tool result is not automatically professional acceptance.

inputs.description: The bounded professional problem or change to work on.
Exact accepted state, candidate identity, environment, interfaces and constraints.

outputs.description: Bounded result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession decision/evidence packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: Partitions, retries, idempotency and duplicate suppression.
Leader election, leases, consensus and coordination primitives.
Distributed tracing, fault injection, recovery and state reconciliation.

references.scope: Current O*NET 31.0 occupational baseline used as external human-work evidence; occupation mappings remain bounded and are not AXM profession identity.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current project state before relying on summaries.
Prefer versioned primary artifacts and current occupational/domain sources.
Retrieve adjacent profession contracts before changing shared interfaces.
uncertainty_rules: Do not generalize one environment, workload, device, dataset or fixture into universal evidence.
Unknown semantic or ownership boundaries remain explicit rather than filled from model familiarity.

skills.description: Define bounded crash, delay, duplication, reorder and partition assumptions before protocol claims.
evidence_required: Fault assumptions and excluded failures are explicit.

skills.description: Define and verify safety/liveness/idempotency invariants for distributed state transitions.
evidence_required: Exact protocol/state model and tested transitions are identified.

skills.description: Design reconciliation, retry, deduplication and rollback/replay behavior after partial failure.
evidence_required: Recovery evidence names exact fault sequence and resulting state.

tools.purpose: Execute deterministic distributed-state schedules and fault cases.
allowed_actions: Inject bounded delay, drop, duplicate, reorder and node failures.
forbidden_actions: Treat simulation as proof of every real-network behavior.

tools.purpose: Reconstruct cross-node event/causal sequences from exact traces.
allowed_actions: Correlate event IDs, clocks and state transitions.
forbidden_actions: Invent total order when evidence only supports partial order.

tools.purpose: Exercise bounded failure conditions in authorized test environments.
allowed_actions: Trigger declared non-destructive faults and capture recovery.
forbidden_actions: Expand into destructive/production fault injection without explicit authorization.
tools.failure_boundary: Environment authorization and blast radius bound execution.

procedures.trigger: A bounded task falls inside this profession's declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted state, candidate, interfaces and expected contract.
Define the fault model and distributed invariants before evaluating behavior.
Perform the smallest evidence-backed implementation/analysis using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus retry, duplication, delay and partition/failure conditions.
Record exact evidence labels, excluded faults, limitations and unresolved unknowns.
Hand product/network/SRE/infrastructure decisions to the owning profession before acceptance.
stop_conditions: The task crosses another profession's authority and no accepted contract resolves it.
Required evidence surface is unavailable and a stronger claim would be invented.

canonical: Validated profession methods, terminology, contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted project-specific interfaces, decisions, evidence and known failures.
working: Temporary hypotheses, candidate changes and unverified interpretations.
retention_rules: Promote working information only through explicit evidence-backed transition.
Preserve superseded contracts and rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.
Respect dependencies and ownership without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Claims name exact candidate/environment and strongest supported evidence label.
Fault-tolerance claims name the exact modeled/tested fault set and never imply stronger network or operational guarantees.
minimum_for_working: Representative success, failure and abstention fixtures pass in materially different contexts.
At least one external human-work baseline and one real project/practice evidence set challenge the body.
Cross-intelligence portability and boundary behavior are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded protocol, replication, retry and distributed-state choices inside declared contracts.
must_consult: Product semantics of consistency/availability, network/infrastructure guarantees, capacity and SRE risk acceptance.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority by professional rank.
Claims outside tested fault models, evidence or authority.

handoffs.when: Consistency/availability tradeoff changes externally visible semantics.
Guarantee depends on transport, topology, capacity or operational behavior.

failure_library.symptom: A distributed guarantee is inferred from happy-path or single-node execution.
checks: Exercise delay, duplicate, retry, node loss and partition cases.
repair_path: Narrow claim and add explicit distributed fault evidence.

failure_library.symptom: Retries create duplicates, overload or repeated side effects.
likely_causes: Non-idempotent operation or unbounded retry policy.
checks: Inject duplicate/retry schedules and inspect resulting state.
repair_path: Add idempotency, deduplication and bounded backoff contracts.

professional_tests.fixture: A request times out after commit and is retried.
expected_observations: Detects ambiguous outcome and prevents duplicate side effect.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Result is idempotent/deduplicated or explicitly unresolved.

professional_tests.fixture: Protocol passes local tests but network partition behavior is untested.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Partition remains NOT_TESTED or receives explicit bounded evidence.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
